statement: When a request is preempted and its ProgressIndex is reset to 0 for KV-cache replay, any cumulative metrics (TotalOutputTokens, TTFTSum) already charged to that request must be deducted at the preemption site; otherwise those metrics are double-counted after the request is rescheduled.
regime: BLIS simulator with KV-cache preemption enabled (total_kv_blocks small enough to force evictions under concurrent decode workloads)
mechanism: preemptForTokens() in sim/batch_formation.go resets ProgressIndex to 0, causing the rescheduled request to re-decode from scratch. executeBatchStep() in sim/simulator.go increments TotalOutputTokens on every decode step. Without a compensating deduction at preemption time, the same output tokens are counted twice. The fix records decoded tokens in PreemptedRequest.DecodedTokens before the ProgressIndex reset and subtracts them in scheduleBatch().
applicability_bounds: Applies to all cumulative scalar metrics that are incremented per decode step (TotalOutputTokens, TTFTSum). Does NOT apply to per-request map entries keyed by request ID (e.g., RequestTTFTs[id]) because map overwrites self-correct on the second recording.

statement: The fix to preemption double-counting is zero-cost in the no-preemption regime: with a large KV cache where preemption_count=0, the corrective subtraction loop in scheduleBatch() never executes, leaving all metrics unchanged.
regime: BLIS simulator with large KV cache (no preemptions)
mechanism: The subtraction code is inside the loop over batchResult.Preempted, which is empty when no preemptions occur. No preemptions means the fix is inert.
applicability_bounds: This principle holds for any fix that is conditional on the preemption event slice being non-empty. It confirms the fix is narrowly scoped and cannot regress the no-preemption path.
